cases.why: the build stops checking each font against its recorded hash. A file damaged in transit -- the file bridge has already done this to PNGs -- is inlined anyway, and a browser answers a bad font by silently using the fallback, so the page looks almost right and every later measurement is taken in the wrong face.

the variable file is declared as weight 400 only, so every 600, 700 and 800 on the page is synthesised bold by the browser -- smeared, wider, and measured differently from the real face, while still being 'Plus Jakarta Sans' to anyone who inspects the element.

the unicode-range goes, so the latin and latin-ext files both claim every character and the browser picks whichever was declared last for all text -- here the smaller latin-ext subset, which lacks most basic letters.
the Google Fonts stylesheet is linked again beside the inlined faces. Nothing looks different, which is the point: the page quietly goes back to asking a third party for its face on every load.
